statement.p: Find a path that traces the circle in the plane y=2 with radius r=3 and center (3,2,3) with constant speed 6.

static.solution:
\bf r\it(t)=\left\lt 3,2,3\right>+3\left\lt \cos t,0,\sin t\right>=\left\lt 3+3\cos t, 2, 3+3\sin t\right>
We need to reparametrize the curve by making a substitution on t=\phi(s), so that the new parametrization \bf r\it_1(s)=\bf r\it(\phi(s)) satisfies ||\bf r\it_1'(s)||=6 for all s. We find \bf r\it_1' using the Chain Rule:
\bf r\it_1'(s)=\frac{d}{ds}\bf r\it(\phi(s))=\phi'(s)\bf r\it'(\phi(s))
Next, we differentiate \bf r\it(t) and then replace t by \phi(s):
\bf r\it'(t)=\left\lt -3\sin t, 0, 3\cos t\right>
\bf r\it'(\phi(s))=\left\lt -3\sin(\phi(s)), 0, 3\cos(\phi(s))\right>
Now, we get: \bf r\it_1'(s)=\phi'(s)\left\lt -3\sin(\phi(s)), 0, 3\cos(\phi(s))\right>=3\phi'(s)\left\lt -\sin(\phi(s)), 0,\cos(\phi(s))\right>
Hence,
||\bf r\it_1'(s)||=3|\phi'(s)|\sqrt{(-\sin(s))^2+(\cos(s))^2}=3|\phi'(s)|
To satisfy ||\bf r\it_1'(s)||=6 for all s, we choose \phi'(s)=2.
We may take the antiderivative of \phi(s)=2 s and obtain the following parametrization:
\bf r\it_1(s)=\bf r\it(\phi(s))=r(2 s)=\left\lt 3+3\cos (2 s), 2, 3+3\sin (2 s)\right>
